To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the T-J boundary interval represents the most severe mass extinction event of the Triassic, (2) the end-Triassy extinction was not selective with regard to taxonomic and ecological traits of individual genera, but (3) taxa with an inshoer preference, taxa inhabiting carbonate substrates, and taxa preferentially found at low latitudes had significantly higher extinction rates than other taxa.

(1) the end-Triasssic mass extinction was a mass extinction in the sense of a significant increase in extinction rate relative to the background extinction rate; (2) the end-Tiassic mass extinction was not a qualitativly new type of mass extinction but an intensification of the background extinction pattern; (3) the end-Triasisc extinction was not selective with respect to taxonomic characteristics but was selective with respect to environmental preferences.
